Commentary.Commentary: We are back with the chase! The umpires make their way out to the middle and are followed by the West Indian players who spread across to take the field after a final pep talk in the huddle. But wait, it’s not resumption time yet! Everyone chuckles as the umpires ask them to make their way back out and wait alongside the ropes. Right then, the time is up and in come all the players. Trisha G and Kamalini G are the openers for India Women Under-19. Jahzara Claxton has the new ball in hand and will start the proceedings. Away we go then!
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, with just 45 runs to chase, India Women Under-19 will be looking to wrap this up in no time and start their title defence in emphatic style! West Indies Women Under-19 will need more than a miracle to pull this game out of the jaws of defeat. India's reply in a bit!

Parunika Sisodia is in for a chat. She says that the plan was pretty simple and given the conditions, they were clear that they wanted to bowl first. Adds that she tried to bowl it up there and let the ball do the talking. Mentions that they always try to keep the morale high on the field.

Parunika Sisodia, Joshitha V J, and Aayushi Shukla were the standout bowlers, sharing 7 wickets. Add to that some spectacular fielding efforts that resulted in three run-outs, and it was a near-flawless display from the defending champions.

The combination of poor shot selection, lack of intent, and indecisive running between the wickets made things easier for the Indians, who were sharp in the field and unyielding with the ball. Only Kenika Cassar and Asabi Callender managed to reach double figures, while the rest of the lineup crumbled under pressure.

The Indian pacers, led by Joshitha V J, set the tone upfront with probing lines and lengths, making it difficult for the openers to settle. Joshitha struck gold in the third over, dismissing both skipper Samara Ramnath and Naijanni Cumberbatch on consecutive deliveries, opening the floodgates for India. From there, it was a steady procession of West Indies batters heading back to the pavilion.

What a dominant performance from India Women Under-19! West Indies' batting collapse was nothing short of catastrophic, with the Indian bowlers completely dismantling their lineup. Bundling them out for just 44 runs in under 14 overs is a testament to India's precision, discipline, and hunger to start their campaign on a high note.

OUT! CAUGHT AND BOWLED! All over for West Indies! A strange end to the innings though. This is fuller, at the stumps, Selena Ross clears her front leg and her weight stays back as she looks to push it back past the bowler. Fails to keep the shot along the ground. Chips it straight back towards the bowler. Parunika Sisodia makes no mistake but does not appeal straight away. She checks with the umpire while going back to her mark. The third umpire is summoned and the replays show that it was not a bump ball and the ball went straight off the bat towards the bowler. West Indies Women Under-19 have been bowled out for 44!

Commentary.Commentary: Drinks! India has been clinical in their approach, tightening the screws on West Indies with disciplined bowling and sharp fielding. The relentless pressure has left West Indies scrambling for answers as wickets continue to tumble. The lack of application from the West Indies batters has been evident, with a few rash shots and poor decision-making contributing to their woes. Commentary.Commentary: Overcast skies welcome the two umpires as they make their way out to the middle. The Indian team gathers in a huddle near the boundary ropes before taking their positions in the field. However, the sight of ground staff on standby with covers near the fence is a bit concerning. Thankfully, the drizzle is light and not heavy enough to delay the start of play. Asabi Callender and Samara Ramnath will open the innings for West Indies Women Under-19. Shabnam will kickstart proceedings for India. A slip in place. Off we go...

We are moments away from the start, but before that, Niki Prasad and Samara Ramnath lead their respective sides out for the national anthems. It will be West Indies' anthem first, followed by the Indian national anthem.

PITCH REPORT - Ed Rainsford is in the middle for the pitch analysis. He starts by saying that the clouds are hovering with the chances of rain up to 60 percent at the moment. Mentions that the boundaries all around are 60 yards and Sri Lanka did well to get past 160 runs in the previous game and the outfield will have dried out a bit more. Concludes that the bowlers will have to use the variations to good use and try not to offer width.

The captain of West Indies Women Under-19, Samara Ramnath says that they were looking to bat first. Tells that this looks like a good batting wicket. Mentions that the spirits are high in the team and it is about backing one's abilities. Adds that it means a lot to them to be here at the World Cup.

Niki Prasad, the skipper of India Women Under-19 says they want to use the conditions and with the overcast skies, DLS could come into play. Adds that they have had a couple of good warmup games and want to carry the momentum into this game. Concludes that she is very happy to be leading the side which is nothing short of living the dream.

Hello and welcome to the final game of the day and the opening clash for two solid sides in the tournament slated as Match 8 of the ICC Women’s Under-19 T20 World Cup, 2025! It’s a Group A encounter featuring the defending champions, India Women Under-19, taking on West Indies Women Under-19 at the picturesque Bayuemas Oval in Kuala Lumpur.
... MATCH DAY ...

After Groups B, C, and D kicked off the 2025 ICC Women's Under-19 T20 World Cup on the opening day, the spotlight shifts to Group A on the second day. Defending champions India will begin their title defence against the West Indies at the Bayuemas Oval in Kuala Lumpur. The venue holds fond memories for the Indian team, as they lifted the Asia Cup there in December last year. The defending champions, led by Niki Prasad, come into the tournament having defeated South Africa and Scotland in their warm-up games. At the forefront of their campaign is right-handed opener Trisha G, whose impactful starts have been crucial to India’s success. Her opening partner and wicketkeeper, Kamalini G, also showed promise with decent knocks in the warm-ups. Alongside them, skipper Prasad and Sanika Chalke will be pivotal in the batting department as India look to secure back-to-back titles. While it is rare to see as many as three slow-left-arm orthodox bowlers in a playing XI, this unique attack has been a vital cog for the Prasad-led unit, with Parunika Sisodia, Aayushi Shukla, and Sonam Yadav playing crucial roles. In terms of pace bowling, Shabnam, Joshitha V J, and Mithila Vinod Vinod will be the key options, with Shabnam bringing valuable experience from playing in the Women’s T20 League in India. As for the West Indies, their campaign in the inaugural edition of the ICC Women's Under-19 T20 World Cup ended in the Super Six stage. They began their warm-up campaign this edition with a defeat to New Zealand but bounced back to edge past Nepal in their final game. The West Indies have always relied on their all-rounders, whether in the senior or junior ranks and across both men's and women's cricket. This tournament is no exception, with their Samara Ramnath-led side looking to tap into this strength. Ramnath, herself an accomplished allrounder, will play a pivotal role with the bat and through her off-breaks. While Ramnath has the experience of playing in the Caribbean Premier League, another key allrounder, Asabi Callender, has experience on the World Cup stage, having been part of the 2023 edition. A top-order batter and a right-arm medium-pace bowler, Asabi also has List-A cricket experience back home in the West Indies. If the West Indies hope to make a deep run in the competition, it will also require players like Amrita Ramtahal, Abigail Bryce, and Jahzara Claxton to click with the bat. Claxton, in particular, will also play a key role with the ball, taking on seam bowling duties. Can Samara Ramnath and her team conjure a spirited display to upset India's apple cart in the opener? Or will the girls in blue kickstart their title defence with a win? We shall find out soon.
